channel.title: Rewind Dynamics — Newsroom & Insights
channel.description: Milestones and long-form perspectives on defence autonomy from Rewind Dynamics — autonomous unmanned aerial systems, precision guidance and tactical platforms.

item.title: Preparing for our first mission test this December
item.description: Everything Rewind Dynamics has built so far has lived in development and simulation. This December we plan to put it to its first real-world mission test — a major milestone for the team. Here's what it means.

item.title: The autonomy decade
item.description: Defence advantage has historically been measured in hardware. That logic is breaking down: between two similar platforms, the decisive difference is increasingly what the platform can do on its own — and that lives in software. Rewind Dynamics on why the next decade of capability is a software question.

item.title: Why the tactical edge belongs to autonomy
item.description: Small, autonomous systems change what a dismounted team can see and do. Rewind Dynamics' view on why the tactical edge — close, cluttered and contested — is where autonomy earns its keep.

item.title: Mass, reimagined
item.description: Small, numerous autonomous systems reopen one of the oldest questions in warfare: what mass is worth. Rewind Dynamics on the exchange-rate problem, why more drones is not a swarm, the two-tier mother–child architecture, and what human command means at scale.

item.title: Navigating without the sky
item.description: Satellite positioning is the first capability an adversary removes, and spoofing is more dangerous than jamming because the system does not know it is wrong. Rewind Dynamics on visual odometry, relocalisation, inertial dead reckoning, and why honest uncertainty matters more than accuracy.

item.title: The case for thinking at the edge
item.description: Modern AI assumes a data centre; defence autonomy cannot. Rewind Dynamics on why intelligence must run on the platform — availability, latency, bandwidth and exposure — and the size, weight, power and determinism engineering that makes it possible.

item.title: Command, not control
item.description: Everyone says a human stays in the loop, but the phrase has stopped carrying information. Rewind Dynamics on the difference between in-the-loop, on-the-loop and in-command — and the specific engineering that meaningful human command actually requires, including at scale.

item.title: The cost curve problem
item.description: Counter-UAS is an arithmetic problem before it is a technical one: you can win every engagement and still lose if each win costs more than the thing destroyed. Rewind Dynamics on detection of small, low, slow aircraft in clutter, discrimination, false alarms, and where autonomy helps.

item.title: The attention problem
item.description: Surveillance rarely fails for lack of sensors — it fails for lack of attention. Rewind Dynamics on the vigilance problem, why autonomy inverts the ISR workflow, learning what normal looks like, and why false-alarm rate matters more than raw detection performance.

item.title: Expanding our engineering facility
item.description: More space, better test infrastructure and room to grow the team — an update on Rewind Dynamics' expanded engineering facility and why keeping the understanding in-house matters.

item.title: Autonomy, with a human always in command
item.description: Autonomy is powerful precisely because it acts on its own — which is exactly why a person must stay in command. How Rewind Dynamics designs for human oversight, safety and accountability in responsible autonomy.

item.title: Commencing development of our first unmanned aerial system
item.description: A milestone for the team: Rewind Dynamics has begun focused development on its first autonomous unmanned aerial system (UAV) — part of our simulation-first, human-in-command approach to defence autonomy.

item.title: Edge AI: why the intelligence has to live on the platform
item.description: For defence autonomy, running AI on the device rather than in the cloud isn't an optimisation — it's a requirement. How Rewind Dynamics thinks about edge intelligence, resilience and staying effective without a constant link.

item.title: Building the founding engineering team
item.description: Great autonomy comes from great engineers. An update on the founding team we're assembling at Rewind Dynamics and the disciplines — autonomy, perception, robotics, embedded systems — we're hiring for.

item.title: The case for trustworthy autonomy in defence
item.description: Trustworthy autonomy is not a luxury — it is fast becoming a requirement. Our view on why defence forces should be able to inspect, adapt and own the autonomous systems they depend on, rather than treat them as sealed black boxes.

item.title: Rewind Dynamics is founded
item.description: In 2020, Rewind Dynamics was founded to design and build autonomous systems — unmanned aerial, precision-guided and tactical — for defence and military needs. Why we started, and what we set out to build.
